ImageDescription.value: Leontocephaline wrapped by a serpent of the Mithraic mysteries, with four wings carrying the symbols of the four seasons, and a thunderbolt engraved on his chest. At the base there are the hammer and tongs of Vulcan and Mercury's cock and . This line drawing is of the figure found at the mithraeum of C. Valerius Heracles and sons (dedicated 190 AD) at Ostia Antica, Italy. Vermaseren catalogue number: CIMRM 312.[1] The identity of the leontocephaline is not certain, but it is almost certainly neoplatonic, and is commonly assumed to be in some way related to Aion/Chronos, Arimanius, Zurvān or Yaldabaoth.

Credit.value: Franz Cumont, TMMM I (1896, Bruxelles: Lamartin), p. 238
